answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring each account to lock a stake before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. If several accounts coordinate, their deposits remain tied up, and provable fraud—such as duplicate claims—lets the protocol slash them. This does not prove that an identity is unique; it makes Sybil influence expensive and risky. For instance, oasis, jade, and basalt could be account names, but each still needs its own locked stake, so multiplying identities multiplies the attacker’s capital requirement.
